description: We are a team passionate about space exploration! After months of research, we identified over 30 locations on Earth that share similarities with the Moon and Mars. Using NASA data, we studied deserts, craters, and extreme environments to find potential testing grounds for future missions. Our goal is to help scientists test rovers, equipment, and technologies on Earth before sending them into space, reducing risks, saving time and costs, and supporting future lunar and Martian bases.
summary: Galactic Pulse is our interactive web app for the NASA Space Apps Challenge that finds places on Earth resembling regions on Mars and the Moon. Users pick a study region from NASA Mars Trek, a Moon region, or their own point, and enter its latitude, longitude, altitude and mean temperature. The app then ranks Earth sites by a similarity score that combines four factors the user can weight: temperature, altitude, latitude band and terrain type. Temperature and altitude can be compared in absolute terms or scaled to each world’s own range, so one of the coldest or highest places on Mars is matched with one of the coldest or highest on Earth. The app also shows a feature explorer for the same landform on Earth, the Moon and Mars, a temperature-versus-altitude chart for every region, elevation profiles drawn in Mars Trek, and a photo gallery of the Earth analogue sites. Data come from NASA Mars Trek (MOLA elevation), the Mars Climate Database and Diviner-type lunar temperatures. A method page explains the scoring and openly flags questionable values, such as Mars temperatures colder than the planet’s surface can reach
details:
What it does. Galactic Pulse is our web app that finds places on Earth that resemble regions on Mars and the Moon. Users choose a Mars Trek study region, a Moon region or their own point, with its latitude, longitude, altitude and mean temperature. The app ranks Earth sites with a similarity score from 0 to 100 based on temperature, altitude, latitude band and terrain type, with user-adjustable weights. It also includes a feature explorer showing the same landform on Earth, the Moon and Mars, a temperature-versus-altitude chart for every region, Mars Trek elevation profiles, and a photo gallery of Earth analogue sites.

Benefits and impact. It helps students, researchers and mission planners quickly see which Earth locations are the best stand-ins for a region on Mars or the Moon, for training and testing equipment, and makes comparing three worlds easy and visual.

Tools. A single HTML file built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with charts drawn in SVG, using NASA Mars Trek (MOLA elevation), the Mars Climate Database and Diviner-type lunar temperatures. It runs in any browser, with no special hardware.

Creativity. Its “planet-scaled” mode matches places by their rank on their own world, so one of the coldest or highest places on Mars is paired with one of the coldest or highest on Earth.

Factors considered. Transparent methods: the scoring formula is shown, approximate values are labelled, and suspicious data, such as Mars temperatures colder than physically possible, are flagged rather than hidden.
